source.work: Next.js App Router docs, linking and navigating
source.paraphrase: Internal navigation uses the Link component so the router can prefetch and transition client-side instead of reloading the page.

invariants.why: A plain anchor to an internal route forces a full document reload and skips prefetching, losing the client-side navigation the router exists for.
invariants.fixHint: Replace the anchor with Link from next/link. Keep anchors for external URLs only.
invariants.avoid: This advisory policy checks actual anchor nodes with literal root-relative href attributes, including expression-wrapped strings, anywhere in JSX. It ignores CMS HTML strings, unrelated attributes, external and protocol-relative URLs. Full reloads and downloads can be intentional; do not promote this suggestion without the project's navigation contract.

source.paraphrase: The App Router owns the document through the root layout. next/document belongs to the Pages Router and has no effect under app.

invariants.why: A Document import inside app/ silently does nothing while suggesting the Pages Router still controls the shell, so document changes never apply.
invariants.fixHint: Move document-level markup into the app root layout and declare head data with the metadata export.
invariants.avoid: Re-exporting next/document from a shared module so app files keep importing it indirectly.

source.work: Next.js App Router docs, programmatic navigation
source.paraphrase: Next routers accept href strings. A template or route helper can make the destination easier to read; concatenation alone is not a correctness violation.

invariants.why: This optional readability policy observes concatenated destinations on recognized Next routers. Valid href strings remain valid; the syntax does not prove an unsafe destination or a typed-route failure.
invariants.fixHint: Use a template or the project's tested route helper when this improves clarity. Validate untrusted destinations under the project's routing contract; interpolation alone is not a security fix.
invariants.avoid: Checks cover imported Router and directly imported useRouter calls or same-block const receivers. Array.push, arbitrary injected push methods, indirect aliases, cross-scope bindings and dynamic receiver ownership are not inferred. Keep project routing safety in a reviewed assertion rather than enforcing a preferred spelling.

source.work: Next.js data fetching docs, time-based revalidation
source.paraphrase: A false revalidation value is an explicit supported choice for an indefinitely cached resource; it does not by itself prove an error.

invariants.why: The syntax does not reveal the intended cache lifetime, so an unconditional block is unjustified.
invariants.fixHint: Set an explicit interval in seconds, or declare the segment dynamic on purpose instead of disabling revalidation.
invariants.avoid: A comment next to false does not make the opt-out explicit. Name the caching intent in code.

source.work: Next.js App Router API reference, useRouter, https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-router
source.paraphrase: In the App Router, useRouter must come from next/navigation, not next/router. Using the Pages Router hook under app throws 'NextRouter was not mounted'.

invariants.why: next/router needs the Pages Router context, which app/ does not provide, so the component throws when it renders.
invariants.fixHint: Import useRouter from next/navigation. Read the path with usePathname and the query with useSearchParams. Shared components that must run under both routers can use next/compat/router.
invariants.avoid: Only the exact next/router literal in a value import, re-export, require or import() inside app/ or src/app/ is flagged. Type-only imports, next/compat/router, next/navigation and files under pages/ are allowed. Components outside app/ that the App Router renders are not traced.

source.work: Next.js App Router documentation, Route Segment Config (https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config)
source.locator: Route Segment Config options and Server Components
source.paraphrase: Route segment configuration exports (dynamic, revalidate, runtime, preferredRegion, maxDuration) and generateStaticParams only apply in Server Components and cannot be exported from a Client Component.

invariants.why: Exporting server route segment options or generateStaticParams from a file marked 'use client' either fails the Next.js build or is silently ignored.
invariants.fixHint: Keep the route segment config and generateStaticParams in the Server Component page or layout, and move interactive UI into a child Client Component.
invariants.avoid: Direct variable exports, function exports, and export list specifiers for dynamic, revalidate, runtime, preferredRegion, maxDuration, and generateStaticParams in 'use client' files are matched. Local unexported variables pass.
